queue.title: Cut panel text now says it was cut: 91 such lines fixed across 28 window sizes. The 67 left are whole tables or controls wider than their pane, which is card d-54.
Seven more unexplained test failures from 9 September, all with logs intact. The same check just found eight for eight were real bugs, so these are worth the same look.
My own quick searches reported missing evidence that was present, three times in one night. Any such search needs a known-positive case run through it before its silence counts.
We and another emulator disagree about one bit of the controller port on every ordinary pad read. Recorded honestly: nobody can show who is right, and no real pin corresponds to it.

queue.title: Two things built tonight can only be confirmed by you looking: that nudging a number changes the picture, and that the raster and bands channels now select on a real build.
The sound chip's interrupt signal should last one line, not until taken. It changes what a real driver hears, so card d-51 asks whether you want to listen first.
From aeon: a watch never catches the sound chip reading an address. The warning half is landed and aeon is told; the full fix needs a contract change and a ruling later.
Sweep wave 1: both measured fixes landed today. Left: two look-at-it questions for you (how an unreadable save is shown; which rule the two address boxes share).
On bank-switching games an address no longer names one byte over time. Needs a contract change, and no current game needs it yet, so it's worth weighing against the other rows first.
